entries.title: One material with two intertwined orders
entries.summary: What happens when light perturbs a charge-density wave? In NbTe₂, ultrafast electron diffraction and broadband transient reflectivity follow electronic and lattice order on their own timescales.
paragraphs: Differential diffraction maps reveal how the response changes between approximately 200 femtoseconds and more than 3 picoseconds after excitation.
Time-resolved peak intensities track the evolving lattice response, including coherent oscillations.

figures.alt: Measured changes in NbTe₂ diffraction: the left half shows approximately 200 fs and the right half shows later than 3 ps after excitation. Red and blue spots show intensity increases and decreases.
figures.title: How NbTe₂ diffraction changes after excitation
figures.caption: Differential diffraction images at approximately 200 fs and later than 3 ps after excitation. Red indicates increased intensity; blue indicates decreased intensity.
figures.label: LIGHT-INDUCED STRUCTURAL DYNAMICS
figures.citation: C. Viernes, S. Netzke, D. Sutarma, R. Zheng, L. Daniel, T. Lott, K. Pichugin, M. Schleberger, P. Kratzer, G. Sciaini. “Tracking Nuclear and Electronic Orders in a Charge-Density-Wave Phase.” Ultrafast Science 6, 0200 (2026).

figures.alt: Published time traces show changes in Bragg and charge-density-wave peak intensities and their two strongest SVD components over the first few picoseconds.
figures.title: Time-resolved diffraction intensity changes
figures.caption: Selected Bragg and charge-density-wave peak intensities, and the two leading singular-value-decomposition components.
figures.label: FOLLOWING THE RESPONSE IN TIME
figures.credit: Peak intensities and dominant temporal components.
figures.citation: C. Viernes, S. Netzke, D. Sutarma, R. Zheng, L. Daniel, T. Lott, K. Pichugin, M. Schleberger, P. Kratzer, G. Sciaini. “Tracking Nuclear and Electronic Orders in a Charge-Density-Wave Phase.” Ultrafast Science 6, 0200 (2026).
